seed: Shannon Byrne Susko, System by System post Hedgehog and BHAG and worksheet Hedgehog Concept and BHAG Validation; Jim Collins, Good to Great; Byron Darlison, Why Does Your Company Exist?; Byron, 27-Sep-2026 (horizon in its own field) and 4-Oct-2026 (X is usually a widget).

slides.title: Your BHAG sits where three circles meet.
slides.support: This is the Hedgehog. You use it to validate the BHAG you already have. Your Core Purpose goes in the top circle. Agree on the other two in turn. Validate the BHAG last.

artwork.alt: Three circles overlap: Core Purpose, Core Business and Economic Engine. Each has its question. The BHAG sits where all three meet: a 10 to 30 year goal with no numbers.

notes: This is the Hedgehog Concept. The BHAG sits where three things meet. They are why the company exists, what its core business is and how it makes money.
The BHAG from the Kick Off was good enough to build execution momentum. A year on, the team validates it in full. They are not creating it from scratch. Only the core business question is new.
The Hedgehog is about focus, not fantasy.
The Core Purpose from the Golden Circle goes in the top circle. Then work through the other two circles in order.
slides.headline: Your BHAG sits where three circles meet.

slides.title: What is your core business?
slides.support: Each leader writes an answer alone. Then share.

artwork.alt: The three Hedgehog circles with the Core business circle highlighted.

body: It is what you can be best in the world at, not what you want to be best at.
Which answer says it most clearly? Stay with it until the team agrees.
notes: Many leadership teams find it hard to say what business they are in. Give it time.

Each leader writes an answer and all share. Ask which one says it most clearly, then wait. Once one leader makes a stand, the others agree or disagree. Keep the discussion going until the team agrees.
Best in the world means real capability, not ambition.
slides.headline: What is your core business?

slides.title: What is your Profit per X?
slides.support: Your economic engine. X is usually a widget from your KFFM.

artwork.alt: The three Hedgehog circles with the Economic engine circle highlighted.

body: If you have agreed on your X, read it aloud and confirm it.
If not, each leader writes an answer. Share, then agree.
notes: Profit per X is the one profit ratio that drives the economics of the core business. X is the unit.
Look at the KFFM. X is usually a widget from the map. When it is not, ask how the team will count it each week.
Profit per employee is not the X unless the company’s business is placing people.
On the first pass Profit per X was a hypothesis. A year of running the KFFM is the test.
slides.headline: What is your Profit per X?

slides.title: What is your 10 to 30 year goal?
slides.support: A blind test of your BHAG. Each leader writes one sentence alone, without looking at it. No date, no numbers. Then share.

artwork.alt: The three Hedgehog circles with the BHAG at the center highlighted.

body: Which one is the BHAG? Stay with it until the team agrees.
Then read your current BHAG aloud. Keep it or replace it.
Record the horizon, 10 to 30 years, beside the sentence.
notes: Only start this step when the team agrees on all three circles.
Each leader writes what they think the company’s 10 to 30 year goal is, and all share. Ask which one is the BHAG, then wait for a leader to make a stand. Do not show the current BHAG yet.
The sentence carries no date and no numbers. The horizon goes in its own field beside it.
Only then read the current BHAG aloud from the One Page Plan. The team keeps it or replaces it. A new BHAG or the same BHAG, well tested: either is a good result.
slides.headline: What is your 10 to 30 year goal?
